title: The paste-from-LLM authenticity tell is dead code end-to-end: the client records it, the server whitelist drops it, the DB can't store it
expected: A single bulk paste (>= 600 chars) into the watched editor reaches the authenticity scorer, docks the score by 65 and lands the submission in 'suspect' so it is held for the ownership-verifying interview (the exact adversarial case the live surface was built to catch).
got: LiveWorkSurface records `paste` events with a char-count `size`, but the session flush route's KINDS whitelist is `open|edit|decision_log|submit` (no `paste`) and its event map keeps only {t, kind, path} (size stripped); the dev_session_events table has no size column and getDevSessionEvents selects only t/kind/path. So `observedBulkPaste` in runEvaluateSubmission — `e.kind === "paste" && (e.size ?? 0) >= PASTE_BULK_CHARS` — can never be true. Because observed sessions also waive all commit-history penalties, a wholesale pasted LLM solution scores 'authentic' on the flagship watched path.
evidence: app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:561-564 (INSERT has no size column) and :530-536 (SELECT t, kind, path only)
suggested_acceptance: Add "paste" to the flush route's KINDS, carry `size` through the route map, the dev_session_events schema and getDevSessionEvents; unit-test that a >=600-char paste event round-trips and lands the eval's authenticity band at 'suspect'.
l2_priority: Paste a 1000+ char block into the live editor, submit, evaluate — assert the authenticity badge docks to suspect (expected today: it stays 'authentic').

title: The evaluation never reads the candidate's actual work: session file contents and the DECISIONS.md text reach no prompt, and the studio has no work-product viewer
expected: An eval Eva can defend to a director cites the candidate's own artifacts: what they wrote, what they logged in the forced DECISIONS.md, how their diff engaged the planted seams. The seed exists precisely so 'the submission is a reviewable DIFF against shared ground truth' (seed_materializer.py docstring).
got: runEvaluateSubmission feeds the chain only commits (EMPTY for sessions), probes, case, role and event metadata (paths/kinds/timestamps). The session's saved file tree (files_json) — including the DECISIONS.md the case forces — is never loaded into any prompt; DECISIONS is checked for EXISTENCE only. reflect_commits runs over a zero-commit context for sessions, so the 'reflection' consumed by evaluate_submission and the authenticity scorer is inferred from nothing (deterministic path: pattern 'big-bang', readBeforeWrite 0.35). No studio component fetches session files either, so Eva cannot even open the work manually. The verdict is process-shape + LLM inference over metadata, presented with score bars.
evidence: app/_lib/devcase-run.ts:409-417 (session: events only, commits=[]) and :437-455 (CLI args: no files)
app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:539-547 (files saved) — no consumer outside the flush route (grep: getDevSession/files_json only in session routes)
suggested_acceptance: Feed the session's DECISIONS.md text + a bounded diff of edited seed files into reflect/evaluate/followups (fenced as untrusted, as reflect.py already does for commit messages), and add a read-only session-files viewer to SubmissionRow/EvalPanel so the human can inspect the artifact behind the score.
l2_priority: Submit a live session with a rich, specific DECISIONS.md; check whether the eval summary, strengths/concerns or follow-up questions quote ANY of its content (expected today: none).

title: The entire dev studio is hardcoded English inside an otherwise Czech workspace
expected: Eva operates the Czech UI (her scored criterion: the internal authoring/eval UI renders correctly in Czech); the rest of the workspace tabs are next-intl translated.
got: Zero i18n in app/features/sub_dev/* — grep for useTranslations/getTranslations finds no match in the directory, while 40+ other feature files use it. The Czech sidebar item 'Vývojové případy' (nav is translated) opens an all-English studio: view headings, blurbs, buttons ('Run automated lifecycle', 'Publish', 'Promote to pipeline'), eval labels, error banners.
evidence: grep useTranslations in app/features/sub_dev → no files (vs 97 uses across app/features)
messages/cs.json:868,878 (nav.tabs.dev='Vývojové případy' — the only Czech the tab has)
suggested_acceptance: Externalize the sub_dev strings into messages/{en,cs}.json (a `dev` namespace) like every other tab; npm run i18n:check passes.
l2_priority: Open the Dev tab with locale=cs and confirm the mixed-language rendering live.

title: No candidate-language control in authoring: the auto path inherits the recruiter's locale, the manual path hardcodes English
expected: Eva (cs UI) hiring an international candidate (Sam, en) can choose the language the case brief/tasks/seed README render in — the journey's exact bilingual pairing.
got: POST /api/devcase/lifecycle accepts body.lang but no UI passes it; it defaults to getServerLocale() — Eva's cs — and the DEVP5 threading renders the candidate-facing brief in Czech for an English-speaking candidate (Czech brief inside English page chrome). The manual path (design_artifacts task) never passes lang at all, so runDesignArtifacts defaults to 'en' — the two authoring paths silently produce different languages, and NeedForm offers no selector.
evidence: app/features/sub_dev/DevTab.tsx:222-237 (lifecycle POST body has no lang) + NeedForm.tsx (no language field)
app/_lib/tasks.ts:107-109 (design_artifacts task: runDesignArtifacts called without lang)
app/_lib/devcase-run.ts:129-145 (lang || "en" default); pipeline/jobfit/devcase/design.py:286-291 (language_directive applied to the candidate-facing narrative)
suggested_acceptance: Add a 'candidate language' selector to NeedForm (default: recruiter locale), pass it on both the lifecycle POST and the design_artifacts task; show the case's language on CaseDetail before publish.
l2_priority: Author a case from a cs-locale session, publish, open the token page with locale=en — assert which language the brief/tasks/seed README actually render in.

title: The live-work submit — the SOLE path for workspace cases — skips the acknowledgement comm and never resumes a collecting auto-lifecycle (and bypasses the closed-posting guard)
expected: Every intake path behaves alike: an ack comm is queued for the candidate and resumeCollectingLifecycle wakes an automated lifecycle so the submission gets evaluated without a human noticing it (the page's own comment promises 'ack comms + lifecycle resume come free').
got: The repo-link form and the inbound webhook go through intakeSubmission (ack comm, closed-posting guard) + resumeCollectingLifecycle. The session submit route calls only submitDevSession: no ack is ever queued, no lifecycle resume fires — an auto-lifecycle sits at 'collecting / awaiting submissions' while Sam's work waits for Eva to click Evaluate manually — and posting.status='closed' is not checked at finalize (only at session start). The page.tsx W5-1 comment describing the webhook path ('ack comms + lifecycle resume come free') is stale for the surface it now fronts. Sam does get an immediate in-UI 'Submitted' confirmation, which keeps this from being a blocker.
evidence: app/api/devcase/session/[id]/submit/route.ts:20-26 (submitDevSession only; no intake/ack/resume; no closed check at :15-16)
app/api/devcase/submit/route.ts:25-34 and app/api/devcase/inbound/route.ts:45-53 (the other two paths: intakeSubmission + resumeCollectingLifecycle)
app/_lib/distribution.ts:77-99 (closed-posting guard + auto-ack live in intakeSubmission, which the session path never calls)
app/devcase/apply/[token]/page.tsx:17-21 (stale 'come free' comment) and :84-88 (live surface = sole submit path when a seed exists)
app/_lib/devcase-orchestrator.ts:261-303 (collecting stage returns 'awaiting submissions' until resumed)
suggested_acceptance: Have the session submit route (or submitDevSession's caller) send the acknowledgement comm, call resumeCollectingLifecycle(posting.id) for new submissions, and enforce the closed-posting guard — ideally by routing finalize through intakeSubmission with repoRef 'session:<id>'.
l2_priority: Run an auto lifecycle to 'collecting', submit via the live surface: does the submission ever get evaluated without a manual click? Is there an ack row in the outbox? (expected today: no and no)

title: The designed timebox (senior = 2.0 h hard cap, shown to the candidate) is 3-4x the <30 min research anchor both characters carry
expected: A brief case (~<30 min of real work) that a strong senior will actually take — the journey's definition of done cites the 40-60% senior drop-off on long take-homes.
got: design.py deliberately pins the timebox at junior 1.0h / medior 1.5h / senior+lead 2.0h with _MAX_TIMEBOX_HOURS=2.0 and clamps the LLM's own longer estimates — a real and valuable brevity gate that kills the half-day take-home (the same research is cited in the code comment) — but the shipped budget is still 2-4x the characters' 30-minute bar, and the number is printed in the candidate-facing brief ('~2h timebox'). Sam's scored criterion rates a long case major minimum.
evidence: pipeline/jobfit/devcase/design.py:26-38 (_MAX_TIMEBOX_HOURS=2.0, _TIMEBOX senior=2.0) and :387-396 (clamp of the model's estimate)
app/features/sub_dev/DevHelpers.ts:47 (timebox rendered into the candidate-facing markdown)
suggested_acceptance: Either lower the cap toward a 30-45 min live-work budget for seed-backed in-product cases (the surface removes setup time, so the old take-home budget doesn't apply), or make the timebox an authoring knob with the research anchor as the default — and validate at L2 that a real generated case is finishable inside its printed budget.
l2_priority: Generate a real senior case from a CS JD and honestly assess: can the 3-4 tasks be done in the printed timebox, and would a 30-min version still carry signal?

title: The 'live work surface' is a single plain textarea — no syntax highlighting, no runner, no way to execute the verification the case itself demands
expected: A production-quality editor/runner (Sam's blocker-level criterion is only 'loads, accepts input, saves' — met — but his senior bar is a surface that doesn't fight him for ~2h of real work, on a case whose verification-trap probe explicitly rewards 'adds real tests / validates').
got: One <textarea> with a file list: no highlighting, no diff view, no test execution, no terminal. The case's own tasks ('make your change safe — show how you checked it') cannot be performed in-surface; a senior will do the real work in a local editor and paste back — the exact bulk-paste behavior the (currently dead, dch-l1-001) authenticity tell penalizes, so the design pushes honest candidates toward the suspicious pattern. Observed verification signal is inferred only from touching test-named files (process_events editedTest).
suggested_acceptance: Either add minimal execution affordance (even a check-my-work button running seed-declared assertions server-side) or scope seed tasks to review/edit/decision work that is honestly completable in a textarea, and say so in the brief; at minimum add syntax highlighting + a monospace multi-file editor component.
l2_priority: Work a real seed for 10+ minutes in the surface: latency of the 8s flush, editing feel, both themes; judge whether a senior would stay in-surface or eject to a local editor.

title: Seed-engagement evidence (planted files touched) is never computed for live-session submissions — exactly the path where the data is richest
expected: The 'Seed engagement: n/m planted files touched' chip — the mechanically comparable evidence beside the LLM read — appears for every submission on a seeded case.
got: seedDiff is derived only from git changedPaths (signals), which is null for session submissions; the observed edit events carry the touched paths and the session even stores the full edited tree, but neither is used, so the chip silently never renders for in-product work.
evidence: app/_lib/devcase-run.ts:497-501 (seedDiff gated on signals?.changedPaths — null for sessions)
suggested_acceptance: For session submissions, derive changedPaths from observed edit events (or diff files_json against the seed) and feed seedDiffEvidence the same way.
l2_priority: Evaluate a live-session submission on a seeded case and confirm the seed-engagement chip is absent.

title: STRENGTH — probe safety by construction: the candidate document is composed from a whitelist, so internal material cannot leak
got: caseToMarkdown emits only title/meta/brief/repoSeed/tasks; coverProbes, reveals, decisionSpace, rubric weights and the role spec are structurally excluded, and the candidate page renders ONLY this markdown ('never render the raw case object here'). On Eva's side the same document is shown as 'what the candidate sees' with internal material in clearly-marked amber Lock panels — copy-pasting the assignment can never leak a probe. assess_tooling additionally sources probe kind/where from the authoritative case, never the model payload.
ceiling: The brief text itself is LLM-written around the probes; a clumsy generation could still telegraph a trap in prose — only L2 reading of a real case can confirm the probes stay covert.

title: STRENGTH — the evaluation surface and pipeline are honest about their own reliability: fail-closed gates, per-step provenance, propagated min-confidence, suspect-holds
got: Auto-approve fails closed on template designs, low confidence, or an absent reality reflection (each with a stated reason); degraded scenario/seed generations are badged and audited distinctly, never as success; EvalPanel shows per-step provenance, the MIN-propagated confidence ('an evaluation resting on a confidence-0.2 signal must not look authoritative'), an authenticity band, probe outcomes, the DECISIONS-kept chip and a 'scores are hypotheses; follow-ups verify' note; suspect authenticity overrides a strong score down to 'hold'; per-submission follow-up questions are minted to verify authorship live. This is the shape of defensibility Eva's director test demands.
evidence: app/_lib/devcase-orchestrator.ts:45-70 (gateApproval fails closed), :168-223 (degraded provenance audited distinctly)
app/_lib/devcase-run.ts:617-652 (suspect → hold with surfaced red flag)
ceiling: Honesty about thin evidence does not create thick evidence — the underlying grounding gaps (dch-l1-001/-002) remain; the surface tells you the read is shallow rather than making it deep.

title: STRENGTH — engineer-grade transparency and intake hygiene on the candidate surface
got: Jurisdiction-aware AI disclosure with a data-consent line on the exact surface where AI evaluates him; the work-surface intro states precisely what is observed ('what you open, what you edit, DECISIONS.md') and what is not ('never keystrokes or your screen') and that AI use is allowed; identity capture requires a validated email with a plain-language why ('the only way we can invite you to the next step'); sessions mint lazily so a reader never orphans one; submit is double-click-guarded, idempotent and atomic; flush failures re-buffer instead of losing events.
ceiling: Disclosure is only as true as the loop behind it — until dch-l1-005 is fixed, 'the team will review it' is a promise the automation doesn't yet keep on this path.

title: STRENGTH — case authoring is genuinely grounded (5/6): real JD body, real multi-repo snapshots, seniority calibration, market-corpus anchors, reviewer feedback
got: The need analysis receives the full JD body (6k chars) + up to 3 real GitHub snapshots and is told to surface stated-vs-real gaps; role design anchors identity to the JD ('the codebase is where this person will WORK, not what defines the role') with comparable seed-corpus roles; case design receives the real stack, true complexity, risk areas and a seniority-scaled hard-capped timebox, demands concrete file/symbol names, bans template phrases, and a redesign honors the human reviewer's note. The dominant AI-product defect (thin grounding) is largely absent on the authoring side.
ceiling: The CV soft-signal focus_probes parameter exists but is not wired through this journey's authoring path (devcase-run.ts:130-150), and grounding quality is only as good as the snapshot (GitHub-only, LOC-probed); keyless runs degrade to templates (scope_note).

title: STRENGTH — the AI-era fairness contract is engineered, not aspirational: AI use is never penalized, and an offline eval harness gates it
got: Every prompt in the chain asserts the code is assumed LLM-generated and AI use is not a negative; over-reliance may only be flagged on concrete evidence, never from tool use (the observed path hardcodes overRelianceFlags=[]); candidate-authored content is fenced as untrusted (prompt-injection mitigation); and submission_eval.py runs measurable gates — verifiers must lead by >=5 judgment pts, AI-verifiers must sit within 2 pts of non-verifiers, strong must beat weak and the AI-no-verify gamer by >=5 — with tri-state inconclusive/not_evaluable semantics so thin samples can't fake a pass. This is exactly the signal both characters say the market lost.
ceiling: The harness certifies the scoring contract offline on synthetic behaviours; it does not run per-submission in production, and the live path's thin grounding (dch-l1-002) limits what the fair scorer has to be fair about.
